newsitem.title: USA: Greenspan gives upbeat assessment of economy.
newsitem.headline: Greenspan gives upbeat assessment of economy.

text.p: Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan on Tuesday gave an upbeat assessment of the U.S. economy but warned of the risks of wage-driven inflation.
He also described the rise in the U.S. stock market as "breathtaking" in testimony prepared for delivery to a Senate Budget Committee hearing on the economy.
Greenspan said the U.S. economy grew about 3 percent last year.
"The economy has retained considerable vigour, with few signs of the imbalances and inflationary tensions that have disrupted past expansions," he said.
"The important question from a monetary policy point of view is whether prospective labour market conditions will be consistent with the maintenance of satisfactory price performance," he said.
In his summary of the economy's performance, Greenspan said: "The stock market continued to climb at a breathtaking rate."
